memo.verdict: Neutral; park, on price, not on quality; conviction medium. Beijer Alma (BEIA.B-SE) at 308.5 SEK on 2026-10-12 is a self-help case inside a serial-acquirer transition whose proved part (the Beijer Components margin repair, the capital redirection to Beijer Tech, the board's targets, six quarters of beats) the shares already pay for at 17.8x 24-month-forward earnings, the 79th percentile of the stock's own history; the unproved part (organic growth; a permanent chief executive) is what is left to earn. The 'Modal return' is 5.8 percent a year over eighteen months and 8.8 percent a year over three years against the framework's 20 percent bar. The gate line does not force the park (no D or F on management, business quality, predictability or trackability); the park is argued from the return (F) and the mark-to-market risk (D). What would progress the case: a price near the ten-year median multiple (about 273 SEK on current consensus earnings; about 255 SEK for a B return on our modal path), or, at today's price, a permanent appointment of a decentralised-model operator together with two consecutive quarters of positive organic growth in Beijer Components. The research base is three months old; the Q3 2026 print on 2026-10-23 is the first thing to read.
case: The thesis. A self-help case inside a serial-acquirer transition, the self-help proved and paid for, the acquirer not yet proved. Since April 2025 the acting chief executive has cut Beijer Components' loss-making tail, taken its adjusted EBITA margin to 20.0 percent in Q2 2026 from 17.8 percent, pointed the group's surplus cash at Beijer Tech and had the board set formal targets; the sell-side has raised numbers for six quarters. At 308.5 SEK and 17.8x the shares pay for the company's own target delivered in full at today's multiple. Material at the inputs and outputs; not material at the price.

Change Forces (E 1, BB 1) B. Internal forces (RA 2) B: standards improvement A (the June 2025 Lesjöfors action plan at MSEK -120 completed in Q4 2025; a SEK 35 million annual savings programme; the R/RK return-on-working-capital metric across 70 companies from October 2025; weekly order and invoicing reporting; 60 to 80 percent of needed price increases implemented; capital efficiency 48.7 percent from 43.0 percent); perimeter reduction A (Alcomex US door springs wound down, SEK 35 million a quarter of loss-making sales in late 2025 and a further SEK 50 million headwind in Q2 2026; Turkish contracts; MSEK 50 of low-margin contracts in Q1 2026; the fire-damaged Åminnefors plant; a Chinese factory into Changzhou; Stumpp & Schüle sold December 2023 at a SEK 107 million loss; every exit loss-making or low-margin so "selling crown jewels" does not fit); chief-executive change B (happened and drove the case, incomplete; the caretaker flag fits on form, not substance: he replaced the Components president in June 2025, closed a factory, wound down Alcomex US, set the targets; the company's six-to-eight-month search window from the Q4 2025 call ran to August to October 2026 with no appointment in files dated October 2026); guidance B (targets above history, a cycle target not a quarter's nudge; no near-term numerical guidance to raise); acquisitions B (disciplined pace and price; the drag is the record: John Evans' Sons USD 61.5 million earn-out fully impaired, Alcomex at about 12x then restructured; the five deals have not reported a full quarter); strategy B (capital to Tech, Components fixes margins before acquiring; a dedicated European components acquisition team not yet proven by a deal); other leaders B (new CFO with segment-level capital-efficiency disclosure; Components senior team cut to six from eleven; Alcomex head office dismantled; no activist); balance sheet B (1.7x after five deals and the dividend; "dangerous leverage" does not fit); new geographies B (first non-Nordic deal, MGA Controls, May 2026; small in money, large in what it proves; not A until a second); price rises B (gross margin up 1.9 points; real in the period, nominal with a lag over a cycle); shareholder returns C (steady, no buybacks, cash kept for deals); new products C (modest, by acquisition). External forces (RA 1) C: demand C (flat; mild headwind in Europe, tailwind in the US and the Nordics; 77 percent of sales general industrial; an expert reading of about 4 percent European recovery by late 2026 not yet in Beijer Alma's orders); own cycle C (reported growth almost all acquired; organic +2 percent Q1 to 0 percent Q2; backlog effect diminishing; tail-cutting ends late 2026); macro C (krona: 76 percent of sales invoiced abroad, a 1 percent move worth MSEK 6 pre-tax, -4 percent revenue headwind in Q1 2026, translation unhedged, Nordea EUR/SEK 10.40 by end-2027; rates: 1 percentage point worth MSEK 25 pre-tax, offset by financing costs falling after the Q4 2025 refinancing); competition B (an acquisition gap left by Addtech, Indutrade and Lagercrantz; Components the only global spring consolidator; Chinese entry reaches commodity lines, not custom); supply B (tailwind; prices set at order on custom work; a steel or energy spike before pass-through is the watch item); political B and disruption B (not material; local-for-local across 19 countries insulates from tariffs except Alcomex's 1 percent of sales).

Financial Outputs (E 2, BB 1) B. Improving on margin and cash, the lines the framework weights most, with the sell-side raising; revenue growth acquired, not organic. Sell-side upgrades (RA 1) B: likely but modest; the 15 percent target sits above consensus EBITDA growth of 8.9 percent FY2027 and 5.5 percent FY2028; the mechanism is announced deals added to models carrying none unannounced (guidance versus consensus B, partly definitional and known); beat record six quarters (Q2 2025 +10 percent, Q3 2025 +12 percent, Q4 2025 in line, Q1 2026 +4.5 to 5 percent, Q2 2026 +3.6 percent; one miss Q3 2024 under the previous chief executive); the acting chief executive's "normalized and not pushed to the maximum" posture; revision skew to raises (FY2027 +9.2 percent over six months, all four brokers raising targets September to October 2026; no count available, so the three-to-one test is inferred); dashboard revisions B with the next leg dependent on Q3 2026 and the Q3 deals; sell-side calls the target "a realistic objective"; our modal forecast C (14.0 SEK FY2026 in line with consensus 14.05 SEK; 15.9 SEK FY2027 below consensus 16.45 SEK on about 1 percent organic and a krona drag; no Viewforth model exists). Key metrics (RA 2) B: margin B rising on every basis (company adjusted EBITA 13.9 / 15.0 / 16.2 percent FY2024 / FY2025 / Q2 2026; FactSet operating EBITDA 17.5 / 18.1 / 19.6 percent; consensus brokers'-basis EBITDA margin 18.3 percent FY2025 to 19.7, 19.9, 20.2 percent FY2026 to FY2028; the easy part, the tail cut, is done and the rest needs volume); cash conversion B (448 MSEK free cash flow, 78.9 percent; consensus 646, 920, 1,006 MSEK against adjusted net income 833, 938, 1,013 MSEK, 78 to 99 percent; through-cycle about 60 percent of EBITA; working capital 24.4 percent of sales against Addtech 18.3 to 19.9 percent); revenue growth C (+17.3 / +4.7 / +7.6 percent FY2023 to FY2025; consensus +7.5, +8.0, +3.8, +3.1 percent; holds in the high single digits only while deals keep coming); net debt C (held, re-used, not a reduction story). Goldilocks growth (RA 3) B: +17 percent FY2026, +14 percent FY2027, 13.4 percent a year FY2025 to FY2028 on our modal; about 10 percent beyond and consensus FY2028 +6.8 percent, FY2029 -0.9 percent on one broker (a coverage artefact of models without unannounced deals); over-extrapolation risk from the 17 percent prints is why marked down not up. Staircase (RA 4) B: near steps B (Q3 2026 on 2026-10-23 with the five deals a full quarter; Q3 deals; the appointment; the FY2026 report in February 2027; capital efficiency crossing 50 percent); mid steps B (Components' first deals under the new mandate; tail-cutting ends late 2026 so organic prints clean; a second non-Nordic deal; the European recovery, exogenous); far steps C (ordinary rhythm; the end-2028 refinancing); the most important step, the appointment, is not in the company's gift to time.
counter_case: Whole case: the false friend. The margin gains are the arithmetic of cutting volume, not of demand or pricing: Beijer Components' margin rose because MSEK 50 of contracts, SEK 35 million a quarter of Alcomex sales and the Turkish business were cut while its organic volume contracted 2 percent in Q2 2026; the ten-year record is a 9 percent return on incremental capital; the 15 percent EBITA growth target sits against an 11 percent five-year record; leverage rose from 0.60x in 2018 to 2.30x in 2024; the board mis-hired a chief executive who left after twelve weeks. The recovery is subtraction mistaken for operating leverage, and when the subtraction ends the organic line shows what is underneath. We concede the volume point, the capital-return record and the leadership risk in full; we cannot show from the printed accounts that Components will grow organically. We hold that the margin is real money (adjusted EBITA 346 MSEK in Q2 2026, +13.5 percent; gross margin 32.6 from 30.7 percent, so pricing is in it), that Beijer Tech's 19 percent return on incremental capital and five-deal quarter are a different engine, and that the price, not the company, is where the case fails: the false friend and our modal path agree the shares do not earn the bar from 308.5 SEK, so the hypothesis changes the reason for the park, not the park. It wins if Components' organic growth is still negative two quarters after the tail-cutting ends in late 2026; that print would take 'Change Forces' to C.

The bull's case, at full force: we are mis-reading a compounder in its first two years. Beijer Alma has every element the cohort's winners had at the same stage: a decentralised model of 70 companies; an operator who built Indutrade from SEK 3.8 billion to SEK 14.8 billion of sales; a division earning 19 percent on incremental capital with a pipeline larger rivals have abandoned; a components division back at 20 percent margins; leverage at 1.7x; six consecutive beats; estimates up 10 percent in six months; a 15 percent discount to peers at 15.7x 2026 EV/EBITA against Lifco, Addtech, Indutrade and Lagercrantz at 22x; a unanimous Buy from four brokers at 350 to 355 SEK; a Stage 2 chart. On this reading our 16.7x blend is a mean-reversion reflex applied to a stock whose mean has moved, the organic flatness is the deliberate price of the margin, the vacancy is a formality while the best operator the company has had is in the chair, and the 10 percent growth we assume beyond FY2028 ignores the arithmetic of 6 percent acquired growth at 8x plus 3 percent organic plus operating leverage, which reaches 15 percent EBITA growth without heroics. We concede: the operating record since April 2025 is first-rate; the capital rule is right; the consolidation gap is real; the balance sheet can fund the pace; our modal may prove low on acquired growth; if the company delivers 15 percent with the multiple held the return is about 20 percent a year, a B, so the bull is not wrong about the company, only about the price at which its case is already in the shares. We hold on three facts the bull does not carry: the record (ten years of 9 percent incremental returns, an 11 percent five-year EBITA rate, a margin decline at Lesjöfors from 2021 to 2024 being repaired not extended, two failed Components acquisitions; the elite peers compounded at 19 to 22 percent a year when they earned 22x, Beijer Alma has done so for six quarters); the price (a 79th-percentile multiple on zero organic growth in a regime bearish on the discount rate, where the target must be delivered in full with the multiple held just to reach the bar); the resource (a case resting on one man's rules is not a compounder's case until a second person has run it, and the board that must choose last chose badly).
triggers: - What would progress the case: a price near the ten-year median multiple, about 273 SEK on current consensus earnings (about 13 percent a year on the blend, a C; about 28 percent on the target path with the multiple held), or about 255 SEK for a B return on our modal path (230 SEK over three years); or, at today's price, a permanent appointment of a decentralised-model operator together with two consecutive quarters of positive organic growth in Beijer Components, moving the blended multiple to about 17.3x, the earnings path toward the target, the eighteen-month return into the C band and the three-year toward B; a delivered FY2026 at or above 15 percent EBITA growth with a chief executive in post would lift the re-rating odds from one in five to one in three.

- What would invalidate or lower: Components' margin below 17 percent, or organic growth below -3 percent (the false friend confirmed; 'Change Forces' to C); a centralised-model appointee ('Foundations' to D) or a second departure; acquired sales below 3 percent of group sales over four quarters or multiples above 10x EBITA (the acquired path to 3 percent, a C on that leg); a euro-area manufacturing index below 48 for two consecutive quarters (the earnings path toward the stress case of about 10 SEK; F throughout); net debt to EBITDA above 2.2x on the company's basis.

- Alarms: a deal-free half-year; Components margin below 18 percent; a third consecutive quarter of negative Components organic growth after Q4 2026; no appointment by the FY2026 report in February 2027; book-to-bill below 1.00x or organic orders below 0 percent; the 24-month-forward multiple below 15.8x with earnings intact (the market moving first); capital efficiency below 45 percent; EUR/SEK below 10.40; net financial items above MSEK -50 a quarter.

- The first thing to read: the Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-23, the first quarter with the five Q2 deals fully consolidated, together with any Q3 deals and the appointment, whose six-to-eight-month window has run.

- Open: whether the permanent appointment arrives and who it is; whether Components' organic line turns after the tail-cutting ends in late 2026; whether capital expenditure below depreciation is underinvestment or the completion of a rebuild; whether the firm's own historical errors and lessons files, not in this record's research, fit the two archetypes named; the missing sector tilt behind the pinned A on Thematic Fit/Momentum; the pattern to watch under red flags is market catch-up, our concern that the compounder label is ahead of the record followed by underperformance.
- Stage note: Part 7 of the Written Summary not written at Triaging; evidence convention A on trial.
